text: Did the student fail because they did not take or pass a required exam?
Did the student fail because they did not complete or pass required coursework other than an exam?
Did the student fail because they missed too many classes, despite being attentive when present?
Was the failure caused by an administrative or enrollment issue rather than the student's academic performance?
Was this a school or university course in the ordinary academic sense?
Was the student taking a practical skills course, such as driver training, rather than an academic course?
Is the student a person?
Was the “course” a course of treatment or therapy rather than a course of instruction?
Does “course” refer to a route or track the student was trying to traverse, rather than a class they were graded in?
Was the student trying to traverse a physical course laid out on the ground?
Was the physical course an obstacle course?
Was the student trying to complete a race course?
Was the student trying to get through a maze?
Was the student trying to complete the physical course as part of a sport or game?
Was the student unable to finish the physical route because something physically blocked the way?
Was traversing the physical course part of a test of the student's physical ability?
Was the student physically capable of traversing the route but not permitted to do so?
Was the student forbidden to traverse the route because it was on restricted or private property?
Was the student denied permission to traverse the route by a person who controlled access to it?
Was the person controlling access a teacher or instructor?
Was the physical route part of a building or facility that the student was trying to enter or leave?
Was the route a road or passage that the student could not use because they lacked a required ticket, pass, or other authorization?
Was the student denied permission to traverse the route by a police officer or other law-enforcement authority?
Was the student stopped by an automatic barrier or checkpoint rather than by a person?
Was the student barred from the route because of who they were or how they were identified?
Was the physical course a route through a natural landscape, such as a mountain trail or river crossing?
Was the route closed to everyone at the time the student tried to use it?
Did a person physically stop the student from going along the route?
Was the student denied permission because traversing the route at that time would have been unsafe?
Was the student unable to proceed because another person was already occupying or using the route?
Was the student trying to pass another person who was ahead of them on the route?
Was the other person approaching the student from the opposite direction along the route?
Was the student traveling along the route in a vehicle?
Was the person occupying the route unable or unwilling to move out of the way?
Was the person occupying the route unaware that the student wanted to pass?
Was the route too narrow for the student and the other person to use it at the same time?
Was the other person deliberately occupying the route to prevent the student from proceeding?
Was the route a walkway intended for pedestrians?
Was the route a track intended for trains or other rail vehicles?
Was the route a road intended for motor vehicles?
Was the route intended for boats or other watercraft?
Was the student trying to traverse the route on foot?
Was the route a bridge the student was trying to cross on foot?
Was the person occupying the route actively engaged in an activity that required them to remain there?
Was the person occupying the route carrying out a task at that particular location, rather than merely traveling along it?
Was the other person working on or maintaining the route at that location?
Was the person occupying the route performing or demonstrating something there?
Was the person occupying the route working there in an official role, such as directing or controlling movement?
Was the other person praying or engaged in another religious observance on the route?
Was the person occupying the route sitting or lying down there?
Was the other person using the route as a place to relieve themselves?
Was the other person interacting with an object or feature located on the route?
Was the person occupying the route engaged in an activity involving an animal?
Was the person occupying the route engaged in a recreational activity?
Was the other person playing a sport while occupying the route?
Was the other person playing golf on the route?
Was the other person playing a game that involved throwing or hitting a ball?
Was the other person playing a sport on the route itself, so the route was being used as the playing area?
Was the other person playing a team sport?
Was the other person playing tennis on the route?
Was the other person playing football (soccer) on the route?
Was the other person riding or driving a vehicle as part of the sport they were playing?
Did the student need to wait for the other person to finish playing before they could continue along the route?
Was the other person playing a sport on an ice rink?
Was the other person playing baseball on the route?
Was the student trying to cross a sports playing area while another person was actively using it for play?
Was the route a sports field or court that the student was trying to cross?
Was the student trying to cross the sports field as a shortcut while a game was in progress?
Did the student have to wait because crossing would interfere with or interrupt the game being played on the field or court?
Was the student trying to cross the field to reach a class or other destination on the far side?
Was the student merely trying to cross the field as a pedestrian, rather than taking part in the game?
Was the student unable to cross because the game continued for the rest of the time they had available?
Did the student miss a time-sensitive appointment or deadline because they had to wait for the game to stop?
Did the student eventually cross the field after the game ended?
Was the student’s inability to cross the playing area the reason they could not complete some separate task or journey?
Was the student unable to cross because doing so would have violated the rules or etiquette of the game in progress?
Was the game being played by students as part of a physical-education class?
Could the student physically have crossed the playing area, but chose to wait so as not to disrupt the game?
Were the student’s intelligence and attentiveness unrelated to why they had to wait?

“Course” means a physical route across a sports field or court, not a class the student needed to pass. The student was walking across the playing area while someone was using it for a game. They could physically cross, but sensibly waited rather than interrupt the game or violate its rules or etiquette. Their intelligence and attentiveness in class had nothing to do with it.
